title: Reward Signal Richness: Per-Dimension vs. Scalar
question: Do per-dimension wiggum scores provide meaningful reward signal beyond the composite scalar for GRPO, or does the scalar capture enough?
hypothesis: depth and grounded together explain >85% of composite score variance across rollouts; the remaining four dimensions add <0.05 Kendall-tau lift over the scalar ranking.
falsified_if: Any single non-depth/grounded dimension has Kendall-tau > 0.25 against a ranking that disagrees with the scalar ranking on >15% of rollout pairs.

decision_rule.use_scalar_only: top-2 dims explain >=85% of composite variance AND Kendall-tau(scalar_rank, composite_rank) >= 0.90 across tasks
decision_rule.use_dim_weighted_reward: any dim has per-task variance >1.5 AND disagrees with scalar ranking on >20% of pairs — build reward as weighted sum matching _DIM_WEIGHTS in wiggum.py
decision_rule.use_top2_dims: top-2 dims explain >=85% but scalar ranking diverges on 10-20% of pairs — use reduced reward = 0.55*depth + 0.30*grounded

method.note: --score-only disables wiggum revision (1 eval pass only); preserves score variance needed for ranking analysis. --limit 20 selects first 20 tasks from bank.

outputs: dim_correlation_matrix.json — Kendall-tau between each dim and composite across all rollouts
dim_variance_by_task.json — per-task std dev for each dimension across 4 rollouts
pca_explained_variance.json — cumulative variance explained by top-K dim components
scalar_vs_dim_disagreement.json — fraction of rollout pairs where scalar rank != dim-weighted rank

controlled.tasks: first 20 entries from tasks/rl_bank.jsonl (all research, hard/medium)

requires: collect_rl_data.py: emit chosen_dims/rejected_dims in grpo.jsonl records (see code note)
analyze_exp_A.py must exist (written alongside this spec)
code_note: collect_rl_data.py emit_grpo() must add 'dims' field per completion, sourced from run_data.get('wiggum_dims', [])[-1] or {}.
